validity.recommendation: The rebuilt Taganrog-Mariupol segment is real and under construction. Its length and diameter are not stated in the pages read.
validity.researcher_notes: A July 2024 report, republished in 2025, says Russia is laying a pipeline from Taganrog to occupied Mariupol. It gives no length of 42.63 km, no diameter of 700 mm and no dates. Those figures stay on the sheet without a ref in this pass.

status_reviews.staleness_rule: Construction row. No source read says it was finished or stopped.
status_reviews.researcher_notes: The July 2024 report says the pipeline from Taganrog to Mariupol is being laid. That fits construction. One publisher only, so the tier stays medium.

wiki_citations_read.note: A November 2014 item quoting the energy minister of the Donetsk People's Republic. It says the Taganrog-Mariupol pipeline was built in the 1950s, has been idle since 2009, and that Donbasstransgaz is restoring it. It gives no length, diameter or capacity.
The page describes the Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine as the certified operator of Ukraine's transmission system. It does not name this pipeline.
An October 2022 article on settlements in Zaporizhzhia region starting to receive gas. The Wayback copy was read and names no pipeline from Taganrog.
The company page of the Ukrainian system operator. It describes a whole national network and does not name this pipeline.

The Ukrainian operator table, read as a June 2022 Wayback copy. It lists Rostov-Taganrog-Zhdanov, 400 to 1000 mm, 516 km, one string, Russia and Ukraine. That is the old line and not the rebuilt segments or the Berdyansk extension on this row. No value is owed from it on this row.
A July 2024 report says Russia is laying two pipelines at once, one from Taganrog to occupied Mariupol and one on toward Berdyansk. It gives no length, diameter, capacity or dates.
Fetching the ministry order redirects to an unrelated online casino page on gazetakursk.ru, so the order could not be read. The Wayback index has no capture.
